headline: Research is shifting from training models to reason toward agents that act, learn from environments and improve themselves, while industry coverage shifts toward safety and security incidents.

cooling.label: RL for verifiable rewards and chain-of-thought

themes.title: Agent training is replacing reasoning-model recipes as the center of gravity
themes.body: Agentic RL and training environments reached 1.04% of new arXiv papers (473 papers, 457 teams) in August to October, against 0.53% in the prior three months (+98%, z 8.4) and 0.12% a year earlier. It sat above its earlier level in all three months, and its monthly share climbed from 0.11% to 1.26% over twelve months. Coding and software-engineering agents rose in parallel to 0.61% (+56%, z 4.5; 261 teams) and the title term 'coding agents' appeared 174 times against 101 expected [field stats]. Meanwhile RL for reasoning with verifiable rewards fell to 0.78% (-24%, z -3.9) and chain-of-thought reasoning to 0.52% (-27%, z -3.5, and -42% against a year ago), both below their earlier level in every month [field stats]. The same RL toolkit is moving from single-answer reasoning to multi-step tasks in environments. Attention agrees [2610.13166]: agentic RL took 7.29% of Hugging Face upvotes, up from 3.65%, while reasoning RL lost attention (1.76% from 2.52%). Confidence is high: three straight months, 457 teams, and the year-ago comparison agrees. A rebound in reasoning shares would refute it.

themes.title: Self-improvement and looped computation are the fast-growing ideas inside training
themes.body: Self-improvement and self-evolution reached 1.05% of papers (+46%, z 5.1; 460 teams), up from 0.40% a year earlier, and its Hugging Face attention doubled to 5.31% of upvotes. The title term 'self-improvement' appeared 125 times against 27 expected, and 'on-policy' 353 times against 214 [field stats]. Distillation rose to 2.19% (+20%, z 3.8; 951 teams) but its attention was flat at 6.24%: routine practice, not a pull. Looped and adaptive-depth models are small (0.26%, 116 papers) but doubled (+122%, z 4.7) and their upvote share more than tripled to 0.91%, though only two of three months were above the earlier level [field stats]. A digest study shows autonomous post-training by frontier models [2610.33624], and another maps where to loop layers [2610.40325]. Confidence is moderate: looped depth rests on a short run.

themes.title: Physical AI is absorbing the share that diffusion and 3D work once held
themes.body: World models reached 1.86% of papers (+46%, z 6.8; 767 teams), 0.35% a year earlier, and vision-language-action models 1.67% (+45%, z 6.3; 679 teams) against 0.44% a year earlier, both above the earlier level in three of three months. Humanoids and locomotion (0.95%, +60%) and robot manipulation (2.26%, +24%) also rose [field stats]. Diffusion and flow-matching methods fell to 1.49% (-18%, z -3.6, -30% against a year ago) with attention halved to 1.62% from 3.14%, and graph learning fell to 0.91% with near-zero attention [field stats]. World models and action policies are taking the generative-modeling effort. The title term 'world action' appeared 133 times against 58 expected [field stats]. A digest example trains robot policies to imagine outcomes [2610.37666]. Confidence is high for world models and VLA, moderate for humanoids, which held in two of three months.

themes.title: Coverage is moving from product launches to safety and security
themes.body: Our pool held 2185 reputable-outlet stories in August to October against 1618 before. Safety and security stories rose to 9.43% of coverage from 5.38% (z 4.6), the only category that crossed the significance threshold [news stats]. The month's most-covered stories fit: OpenAI cutting ties with three safety researchers (19 outlets) and OpenAI saying its agents weakened an internal monitoring system (5 outlets) [news stats]. A backdoored coding extension on Cursor's marketplace that exposed up to 5,000 developers illustrates the supply-chain side [2026-10-31-n1]. This matches the research surge in coding agents (0.61% of papers, +56%, z 4.5), since agent tooling now carries real attack surface [field stats]. Products and agents (12.54% against 12.92%) and model releases (3.66% against 3.21%) were flat, so launches did not cool; safety simply gained space. Confidence is moderate: one three-month window, and a fixed search pool measures movement but not absolute levels.

themes.title: Compute cost pressure shows up as research on serving and distillation
themes.body: Data centers and energy coverage rose to 9.24% of stories from 7.17% (z 2.3) and funding to 6.68% from 5.69% (z 1.3); both are below the significance bar, so they are context, not a trend. The most-covered story of the month was an aerial look at the data-center boom (33 outlets) [news stats]. The significant movement is on the research side: KV cache, decoding and serving papers rose to 0.94% (+30%, z 3.5; 412 teams, above the earlier level in three of three months) and distillation to 2.19% (+20%, z 3.8; 951 teams), both roughly double their year-ago shares [field stats]. Digest coverage shows the strain that could explain it: Alphabet lost about 500 billion dollars in market value as AI spending turned its cash flow negative [2026-10-30-n2], while Microsoft reported Azure growth of 48% [2026-10-29-n2]. The link between spending worries and efficiency work is plausible, not proven; Chips and compute coverage stayed steady at 13.55% (z 0.7). Confidence is low to moderate.

themes.title: Attention is concentrating on a few labs while xAI recedes
themes.body: xAI fell to 2.97% of company mentions from 6.80% (z -5.6), the largest company-level change and the only one beyond the threshold [news stats]. OpenAI (17.57% against 17.31%) and Nvidia (11.30%, z 1.1) held steady. Anthropic slipped from 11.62% to 10.02% and Mistral from 1.48% to 1.01%, but both are within noise (z -1.6, -1.3) [news stats]. Open-weight releases did not change the balance: Mistral's trillion-parameter weights drew little relative coverage [2026-10-30-n1]. Confidence is low: the xAI drop is statistically strong, but with a fixed search pool it may reflect a quieter month rather than lost standing, and there is no earlier summary to confirm persistence.
